scope.question: Does the release EXE of 0.2.7, built by CI with Visual Studio 2026, link the same Microsoft runtime families as the build examined on 2026-09-12, and do the Visual Studio 2026 terms change what is delivered?

exe.path: aidevbridge.exe in the ZIP, equal to release-manifest.json native.exe

environment.msvc: Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Tools.x86.x64 18.11.12301.404 (default MSVC 14.51); side by side VC.14.44.17.14.x86.x64 and VC.14.29 (v142), not used by this build (Rich header)
environment.vc_runtime_mode: build.windows.staticVCRuntime true in src-tauri/tauri.release.windows.json (libvcruntime and libcmt linked, UCRT imported); scripts/release-windows-artifacts.mjs rejects RUSTFLAGS and STATIC_VCRUNTIME overrides

tools: own PE reader for Rich header, import, delay-import and debug directories
pe.imports_compared: 22 names on 2026-09-12. New: imm32.dll and api-ms-win-core-winrt-error-l1-1-0.dll (Windows system DLLs) and the upper-case ADVAPI32, KERNEL32, WS2_32 entries of a second import library. The same seven UCRT API sets.

strings.EmbeddedBrowserWebView.dll: UTF-16, statically linked WebView2 loader of webview2-com-sys 0.39.1

rich_header.meaning: prodid 147 Implib900, 255 Cvtres 14.x, 257 Implib 14.x, 258 Linker 14.x, 259 MASM 14.x, 260 C 14.x, 261 C++ 14.x, 1 imports, 0 unmarked objects

local_comparison_build.description: local comparison build of 2026-11-03, Visual Studio 2022, MSVC 14.44.35207, linker 14.44

reading: The prebuilt runtime objects carry the build of their toolset's libraries, not the compiler build: 35207 locally (toolset folder 14.44.35207, compiler 35229). On 2026-09-12 the PDB of a 14.44 build mapped 46 libcmt and 23 libvcruntime modules, 69 in all; the local group has 9 + 13 + 47 = 69 objects.

The release group has 9 + 13 + 46 = 68 objects at build 35721. Of the toolsets on the image, 14.44 would show 35207 and 14.29 a 30xxx build; 35721 lies below the 14.51 compiler build (at least 14.51.36231 per the 18.6 release notes, here 36260). The group is therefore the libcmt/libvcruntime of the default MSVC 14.51.

The 12 C objects with the compiler's own build are ring 0.17.14's C sources (the only cc-built crate whose objects reach the EXE; embed-resource and vswhom-sys run at build time). Cvtres is the app resource.

Limits: the Rich header proves tool categories and counts, not library names; the one-object difference (68 against 69) is not explained; the six WebView2 loader objects of 2026-09-12 appear in no MSVC row, presumably not built by MSVC (not verified).

sources.title: GitHub runner images: Visual Studio license on hosted runners
clauses: We use an `Enterprise` license key, which, as agreed with Microsoft, is the version for public and private use on `GitHub Actions` and `Azure DevOps` `Hosted Runners`. ... Users do not need to maintain a separate personal copy of the license.

decision.selection: Unchanged: no VC++ redistributable, no Microsoft DLL, LIB or merge module, UCRT as part of Windows 10/11, WebView2 downloadBootstrapper for NSIS and MSI, the same WebView2 SDK and Evergreen texts.
decision.license_basis: The CI build uses the Visual Studio Enterprise installation that GitHub licenses for hosted runners. The linked libcmt/libvcruntime output is distributable under the Visual Studio 2026 Distributable Code terms as Microsoft's licensing guidance reads them; the terms require no Microsoft notice. aidevbridge keeps its own attribution notice voluntarily.

notice.change: "from the MSVC 14.44 toolset" becomes "from the Microsoft C++ (MSVC) Build Tools": the runner label windows-2025 floats and updates the toolset; the exact version belongs in this report and in the version of native:msvc-windows-runtime.

decision.native_import_family_review: Done for 0.2.7 at the level of the import table and the Rich header; the manifest of each build keeps reporting it as pending.
decision.pdb: From this change on, packages.yml keeps the PDB of the Windows build as the workflow artifact windows-symbols (90 days), not as a release asset, so that a later toolset change can be mapped module by module. The PDB of 0.2.7 is gone.

remaining: The use of Visual Studio on hosted runners rests on GitHub's public statement, not on a published license document; the Build Devices clause of the terms does not name third-party hosted machines.
The Distributable List does not name libcmt or libvcruntime; that linked output may be distributed comes from Microsoft's licensing guidance and C++ documentation, as for every MSVC-built program.
Distribution requirement (ii) (terms that protect the Distributable Code) is met in practice only by the notice; the ZIP has no agreement step.
Installer items of the manifest (nsis_msi_payload, installer_terms_ui, installer_stub_notices, product_and_windows_acceptance) are unaffected and stay open.
